body:
**What does this PR do?**

Add and verify opt-in loop experiments A–F with reproducible correctness checks, timing scripts, raw evidence, and one report. The measured gains support narrow follow-up work; general ordered replication does not justify a default change. Native ARM64 execution remains incomplete because hardware is unavailable.

**How does this PR do it?**

Separate bounds treatment, grouping, and accumulator chains for integer sums. Use a bounded Wasm loop plan to replay operations in their original order or lower guarded four-lane maps through each target's existing 128-bit SIMD emitter. Preserve scalar fallback, memory32 wrap, writes before traps, original trap positions, and live exit values.

**What changes are made/proposed?**

- A/B: sum variants A–H and narrow i32-add, integer-XOR, equivalent counter-update, and tee/drop forms.
- C/D: ordered scalar factors 2/4, guarded factor 2, and fixed-width Wasm SIMD factors 2/4.
- E: separate f32/i32 maps with widened range and overlap guards. Both conservative and modern CPU-feature comparisons use identical inputs and matched feature masks. Floating point multiply and add remain separate.
- F: shared legality with separate ARM64 lowering, qualification tests, and a native timing harness; checked ARM64 cross-build passes.
- Bound source/native growth and fall back to original compilation when a bound fails. Retain negative cases, allocator/frame/native-size evidence, input hashes, independent review fixes, and serial reproduction scripts.

**Deltas**

Fixed main base: `2286d676facdfa1cabe2d1c61072e505438ca7f2`. No rebase was used. AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS, Go 1.27.1, Linux; six alternating serial samples per benchmark. All gains below refer to 8192 elements unless stated otherwise.

| Default compiler vs fixed main | Result |
|---|---|
| Existing sum execution and compilation | No significant change |
| Large function with no eligible loop, compile | **+2.16%** in a 12-sample follow-up; allocation counts and bytes unchanged |

Prototype comparisons use the same input and matched reference path on the experimental compiler; they are not claimed as improvements over main's already optimized paths.

| Matched prototype comparison | Significant result | Cost or limit |
|---|---|---|
| Sum B vs A: whole-range proof, factor 1 | **−42.93% execution time** | The combined on/off switch is not a pure unrolling control |
| Sum F vs A: proof, factor 4, four chains | **−70.59%** | Matched grouped-emitter H separates setup from grouping; F vs same-factor single-chain D saves **47.61%** |
| Broader i32 addition / XOR reductions | **−69.43% / −63.80%** | No useful added coverage in the nine sampled corpus modules |
| Modern-feature 128-bit i32 map | **−47.89%**, streaming **−45.42%** | Compile **+165.83%**; native bytes 254→703; about **12 calls** to repay compile cost |
| Modern-feature 128-bit f32 map | **−34.59%**, streaming **−30.76%** | Compile **+167.58%**; native bytes 246→687; about **19 calls** to repay compile cost |
| Conservative SSE2 i32 map | **+221.41% slower** | Four scalar multiply lowering; CPU-feature profitability matters |
| Fixed 128-bit Wasm SIMD, factor 4 | **−8.98%** | Compile **+96.47%**, native bytes 262→544 |
| Real corpus sum, generic count2/count4/guard2 | **+196% / +213% / +232% slower** | Replaces main's already good specialized four-chain sum |

Map gains and the main negative controls have `p=.002`; SIMD4 has `p=.009`. The compile follow-up has `p<.001`. At 8192, direct native execution medians are **0 B/op and 0 allocs/op**. Compiler allocations for maps increase from **26160 B / 30** to **32632 B / 55**. Short-count overhead, isolated small dependent-loop gains, nonzero allocated-byte medians at other sizes, and noisy whole-command startup results are retained in the report.

Read [REPORT.md](experiments/loop-unroll-vectorization/REPORT.md) first. It links exact commands, 1145 benchmark rows with six samples each, 38 verified subprocess groups, native code and assembly, coverage, limits, and promotion decisions. [REVIEW.md](experiments/loop-unroll-vectorization/REVIEW.md) records independent correctness and measurement reviews and their fixes.

**Validation and remaining limits**

- Passed `just test unit` (ordinary and checked builds), the full checked `bench` module, conservative and modern focused experiment suites, guard-page runtime/API tests, `just lint`, and `just docs`.
- Tests include full 4 GiB memory32 wrap, unaligned final-boundary accesses, overflow in large trip ranges, writes before traps, precise original trap positions, partial overlap, tails, NaN rules, live exit locals, and native-growth fallback with one/two compiler workers.
- **Native ARM64 correctness/performance is unverified.** Cross-compilation establishes build compatibility only. The native OS/architecture matrix remains for CI.
- Native per-loop sampling is blocked by OS perf permissions (`perf_event_paranoid=3`); the failure is saved. Module timings and bounded recognition counts are not a dynamic hot-loop ranking.
- Claude Code access failed with `Not logged in`; no Claude review occurred. Independent GPT reviewers inspected the actual diff and evidence.

@JairusSW, please review the semantics, measured costs, and proposed promotion limits.

**Checklist:**
- [x] I've added proper tests. All fixed bugs have a corresponding test
- [x] I've read the contributing guidelines
- [x] My name and email are already in NOTICE (Joshua Tenner)
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG
- [x] I use an LLM to assist with this PR
